pairs.why: B's camera sits high enough to show a large open table top and the ground sweeping back like the real card, while A drops to a lower, closer view with a shallow top face.
B is turned a little more to three-quarter with its strap behind and the roll's top surface visible, like the real pack, but both are close to frontal so the call is weak.
The real clock is a flat, front-on wall piece with a soft shadow on the wall, and A matches that, while B stands it on a floor plane with a horizon and a ground shadow.
Both are similar three-quarter floating objects in front of a flat patterned background, and I see no camera or depth difference to choose between them.
B shows a slightly wider table top seen from higher up, nearer the real card's high camera, though A and B are otherwise very similar.
B shows slightly more of the slab's top surface and a hint of turn, closer to the real pump's high three-quarter view, but both are mostly frontal and low.
B shows the brim as a clean ellipse seen from above with mild perspective, like the real cap, while A's brim and underside look wide-angle and forced.
A gives a close three-quarter front view with the face turned to the camera and a modest top face, like the real bus and coaster, while B is a distant side-on profile.
